title: Staggered-window export reconciliation with stable preview URLs and resumable CSV assembly
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Background: Scheduled customer usage exports are produced in staggered time windows to reduce peak pressure on ingestion and the export pipeline. Currently we assemble CSVs in a single-run worker; if a window runs long or the staging upload fails, customers get missing rows or broken preview links. Goal: implement a reconciliation-first export path that supports staggered window checkpoints, durable resumable CSV assembly, and stable preview URLs that remain valid until the final export is published.
acceptance_criteria: Exports may be composed from multiple staggered window jobs without duplication and with deterministic row ordering per tenant.
Preview links generated immediately after an initial partial upload remain valid and point to an incrementally-updated preview until final publish; preview link tokens are revocable.
Worker restarts, transient S3 upload failures, or partial DB replication do not produce data loss; pipeline resumes from last checkpoint and completes assembly within SLA.
End-to-end tests exercise an interrupted upload and validate final CSV parity against canonical query results.
Operational metrics for checkpoint lag, rows-reconciled, and preview-stale-duration are emitted to the console dashboard and alerts are wired for >5m checkpoint lag.
Migration is backward compatible with existing scheduled export subscriptions and does not change contract URLs for existing final exports.
notes: Tradeoffs: strong consistency per-tenant requires transactional checkpoints in export ledger; full strict serializability is expensive but we can achieve practical determinism by using export_sequence numbers and per-window high-water marks.
We prefer S3 multipart uploads for large CSVs and will use an intermediate manifest object to compose parts from staggered workers rather than reuploading whole CSVs on every resume.

Preview links will point to a versioned preview object (preview-v{n}) stored in a customer-preview bucket with short-lived signed URLs for downloads and a longer-lived metadata record in DB for link discovery.
Security: preview objects are encrypted with customer KMS keys when tenant-level KMS is enabled; preview metadata access will respect RBAC rules in the console.
tasks: Design schema: export_ledger table with (export_id, window_id, sequence_start, sequence_end, rows_hash, state, checkpoint_timestamp).
Implement producer: staggered-window job that writes part-manifests to export_ledger and pushes SQS job for assembler.
Assembler service: idempotent composer that reads manifests, validates rows_hash, patches multipart upload parts, and marks windows reconciled.
Preview link flow: generate preview manifest and signed URL, record preview version in exports.preview_versions table, implement revoke endpoint.
DB migration: add export_ledger and preview_versions tables (backfill lightweight indices for active subscriptions).
Metrics & alerts: add exporter.checkpoint_lag, exporter.rows_reconciled, exporter.preview_stale_seconds metrics; wire PagerDuty for checkpoint_lag > 5m for high-traffic tenants.
End-to-end test: flaky-upload simulation harness (network errors, worker restarts) and integration test validating parity with canonical query.
Create runbook: sequence for manual reconciliation and forced reassembly for on-call use.
